verses.commentary: The Lord showed me. Amos receives visions, not just words. Locusts swarming after the king's harvest. The timing is cruel: royal tribute already taken, now locusts devour what remains for the people.
Sovereign Lord, forgive! Amos intercedes. How can Jacob survive? He is so small. The prophet who thunders judgment also weeps for mercy. Smallness evokes compassion.
So the Lord relented. This will not happen. Intercession succeeds. The first vision shows a judgment averted. God responds to prophetic prayer.
The Lord was calling for judgment by fire. Second vision: cosmic fire that dries the great deep and devours the land. More severe than locusts. Elemental destruction.
Sovereign Lord, I beg you, stop! Same intercession. How can Jacob survive? Same appeal to Israel's smallness. The prophet pleads again.
The Lord relented. This will not happen either. Second vision also averted. God responds again. But the pattern cannot continue indefinitely.
A plumb line in his hand. Third vision: no natural disaster but a builder's tool. God measures his people against his standard. The wall was built true; now tested.
What do you see, Amos? A plumb line. I am setting a plumb line among my people. No more sparing. The testing begins. This time no intercession is offered. The measurement itself is judgment.
High places of Isaac destroyed. Sanctuaries of Israel ruined. Sword against the house of Jeroboam. Royal and religious structures fall together. The plumb line reveals crookedness everywhere.

Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam. The establishment counterattacks. The royal chaplain reports the prophet as a political threat. Amos is raising a conspiracy. True prophecy looks like treason.
Amos is saying: Jeroboam will die by the sword. Amaziah's summary of the preaching. Accurate but incomplete. He reports threat but ignores the call to repentance.
Get out, you seer! Amaziah expels Amos. Go back to Judah, earn your bread there. The accusation: Amos prophesies for profit. Return to your own country. Foreign troublemaker dismissed.
Don't prophesy anymore at Bethel. The king's sanctuary, the temple of the kingdom. This is crown property. State religion has no room for independent prophets.
I was neither a prophet nor prophet's son. Amos denies professional status. I was a shepherd and a tender of sycamore figs. A farmer, not a guild member. No seminary, no credentials, no salary.
But the Lord took me from tending the flock. Divine conscription. Go, prophesy to my people Israel. The call came uninvited. He speaks not for bread but because God commanded.
Now hear the word of the Lord. Amos turns the tables. You say do not prophesy. But silencing the prophet brings judgment on the silencer.

Your wife will become a prostitute. Amaziah's family devastated. Sons and daughters killed. Land divided. Amaziah himself dies in a pagan land. Israel goes to exile. The one who rejected the word receives the word's full weight.
